title: Five heads in a row. Tails is due?
hook: After a streak, it feels like the coin owes you the other side. Does it?

knows: a fair coin lands heads half the time
a percentage as a chance out of 100

misconception: After five heads in a row, tails is more likely next because the coin has to even out.
objective: The learner can explain that each flip of a fair coin is 50/50 whatever came before, and that long-run shares settle by dilution (new flips swamp a streak), not by the coin correcting itself.

claims.text: For a fair coin, the chance of heads on the sixth flip is 50%, even after five heads in a row.
claims.source: Fair flips are independent: P(H6 | H1..H5) = P(H1..H6) / P(H1..H5) = (1/64) / (1/32) = 1/2.

claims.text: In a long run of fair flips, about 1 position in 32 comes right after five heads in a row, so 10,000 flips give roughly 300 such moments.
claims.source: P(the five flips before a given position are all heads) = (1/2)^5 = 1/32; 10,000/32 = 312.5 (overlapping runs count again). Correction to the brief, which said 1 in 64 and about 150: 1/64 is the chance of six heads, not of five heads followed by anything. Seeded stage: 321 cases in the first 10,000 flips.

claims.text: The flips on the stage come from a seeded generator where each flip is an independent 50/50 draw; the share of heads after five heads wanders near 50% and does not lean toward tails.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/five-heads-then-what/model.ts, seed 5150. Re-run with node --experimental-strip-types: after 1,101 flips 21 heads of 39 cases (54%); 2,000 flips 38/75 (51%); 10,000 flips 159/321 (50%); 20,000 flips 341/667 (51%).

claims.text: Over many flips the share of heads settles toward 50% because new flips swamp any streak, not because later flips correct it.
claims.source: Five extra heads shift the heads share of n flips by at most 5/n (0.05% at 10,000 flips), while each new flip stays 50/50; the law of large numbers (Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, Vol. 1, ch. X) gives convergence of the share without any compensation.

recall.question: A roulette wheel has landed on red eight times in a row. On a fair wheel, what happens to the chance of black on the next spin?
options: It goes up: black is due
It goes down: red is hot
recall.why: The wheel has no memory. Each spin has the same chances whatever came before; streaks even out only because later spins swamp them.
